answer: An identity registers by posting a 500-token bond locked for 30 epochs and bound to one hardware credential per device serial, which the registry records as an umber entry. Each fake identity therefore locks 500 tokens for 30 epochs, with 100 percent slashed on proven duplication. Copying a serial adds no gain, because the shared bond takes the full penalty and independent jurors trace the duplicate, while the marginal delta per fake identity stays at 500 tokens and the gale of new registrations never lowers it.
